Embo launches with a $110 million seed round for robot world models

a16z leads funding for an approach combining video learning and practice in imagined scenarios; standardized performance results remain absent.

Embo ↗23 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Funding and investors

Embo introduced itself on November 23 with a $110 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz, alongside Khosla Ventures, DST Global and NVIDIA. It aims to develop robot AI models that handle unfamiliar objects and situations more effectively.

Learning physics and practicing skills

The approach pretrains on large amounts of video to learn physical relationships, then uses experience from a humanoid fleet and reinforcement learning. World models supply imagined scenarios for motor-skill practice, potentially extending training beyond situations covered by task-specific demonstrations.

Claims still requiring evidence

The team cites experience with Dreamer, VideoGPT and Diffusion Forcing. The launch announcement, however, supplies no standardized comparisons, task-success rates or commercial availability date. Team experience and funding support development; they do not establish that reliable general-purpose robot performance has already been achieved.
